title: Orange Chicken
subtitle: crispy air-fried chicken in a sticky, sweet orange sauce — the takeout classic, not spicy
imageAlt: Crispy chicken pieces in glossy orange sauce beside white rice with a twist of orange peel
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

breakdown: Brown sugar, soy, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger

beforeYouStart.text: Frozen chicken? Thaw in the fridge overnight.
Start the rice before you bread the chicken.
Preheat the air fryer to 200°C (400°F) for 3 minutes.
Zest the oranges before you juice them — zest is where the big orange flavour is.

items.name: canola or vegetable oil
items.note: in a spray bottle or brushed on

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Season and coat
steps.text: Pat the chicken dry and season with salt, pepper and garlic powder. Toss in the beaten egg. Mix the cornstarch and flour in a bowl, then toss the chicken in it a few pieces at a time, pressing so every piece is fully coated. Shake off the extra.

steps.title: Air-fry until crisp
steps.text: Spray or brush the pieces with oil. Air-fry in 2 batches in a single layer at 200°C (400°F): 6 minutes, shake and spray any floury spots, then 5–6 minutes more until golden and 74°C (165°F) inside.

steps.title: Make the orange sauce
steps.text: While batch two cooks, simmer the orange juice, orange zest and juice, brown sugar, soy sauce, rice vinegar, garlic and ginger in a large skillet over medium for 3–4 minutes. Stir in the slurry and simmer 1 minute until thick and glossy.

steps.title: Toss and serve
steps.text: Turn off the heat, add the crispy chicken and toss 20–30 seconds just to coat — toss right before eating so it stays crunchy. Serve over the rice.

fixIt.fix: Spray any dry floury spots with oil when you shake the basket — dry flour stays white and powdery.
Simmer another minute; add ½ tsp more cornstarch in 1 tsp water if needed.
Add 1 tsp more rice vinegar and a squeeze of fresh orange.
Sauce went on too early. Keep sauce and chicken apart until the last minute; leftovers re-crisp in the air fryer.

saleTip: No Frills' chicken breast club packs drop to ~$9–10/kg on flyer weeks; navel oranges are often 3 lb for $4 in winter.
swap: Chicken thighs (air-fry 1–2 min longer) or shrimp (air-fry 6–7 min). No air fryer: bake on an oiled rack at 220°C (425°F) 15–18 min, flipping once.
leftovers: Fridge 3 days, sauce and chicken in separate containers if you can.
source: Based on tested copycat orange chicken methods (Panda Express-style, adapted for the air fryer by Allrecipes and Tasty test kitchens): egg + cornstarch coat, orange juice + zest sauce thickened with cornstarch.
prepAhead: Cut the chicken a day ahead and keep covered in the fridge.
Mix the orange sauce (without the slurry) up to 3 days ahead.
reheat: Air fryer 180°C (350°F) 4–5 minutes to re-crisp, then warm the sauce and toss. Microwave works but softens the coating.

basic.note: Crispy chicken with an orange juice glaze — no zesting, fewer spices.

1-0.note: from the carton — a little extra since there's no fresh orange

stepNotes.3: Basic: orange juice, brown sugar, soy and garlic.

fancy.note: Extra-crisp chicken in a bright fresh-orange glaze with candied zest and sesame.

stepNotes.3: Fancy: add the honey and simmer 1 minute longer for a glossy glaze.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Lay thin orange wheels around the plate, pile the rice and chicken in the middle and finish with sesame seeds and a little extra zest.

plating: Thin orange wheels around the rim.
Chicken piled high in the middle.
A little extra zest over the top right before serving.

why.1-1: Fresh zest gives the real orange flavour; juice alone is sweeter and flatter.
why.1-7: Cornstarch thickens the glaze so it clings to the crispy chicken.
why.0-5: Cornstarch in the coating is what makes it crunchy.
